web_fixture.snippet: Every gateway error kelpgate can return, each with the condition name our field guides use and the recommended handling.
web_fixture.content:
# kelpgate error codes

Every error the gateway returns carries a code of the form KG-NNNN. This reference lists each code, the condition name our field guides use, and the recommended handling.

## Client and handshake conditions

| Code | Condition | Handling |
| --- | --- | --- |
| KG-4001 | deadpipe | The client closed the connection partway through sending the request body. No action needed. |
| KG-4010 | overrun | The request exceeded the per-route burst allowance. Shed load or raise the route budget. |
| KG-4021 | sealbreak | The upstream peer closed the connection partway through the TLS handshake. The listener marks the route unhealthy until a probe succeeds. |
| KG-4033 | halfwake | The upstream accepted the connection but never sent response headers. Check upstream saturation. |
| KG-4044 | slowdrain | The response body trickled below the minimum drain rate and was cut off. |

## Server conditions

| Code | Condition | Handling |
| --- | --- | --- |
| KG-5001 | backwall | The upstream returned an unparsable response. Report it with the response dump. |
| KG-5011 | drywell | No healthy upstream was available for the route. |

Last reviewed 2026-06-19.

web_fixture.title: kelpgate KG-4021 after every gateway upgrade
web_fixture.snippet: Our fleet throws KG-4021 in bursts right after a rolling restart, then it settles. Has anyone pinned down the reason?
web_fixture.content:
# kelpgate KG-4021 after every gateway upgrade

**posted 2026-01-27 by Nadezhda Ferrers**

Every time we roll the gateway fleet, a handful of routes start returning KG-4021 for a few minutes and then settle. The upstreams are healthy the whole time, so I do not think it is capacity.

**replied 2026-01-28 by Tobias Grangier**

We saw the same pattern. During the roll the listener still holds the previous upstream health entry and keeps rejecting the new peer until a probe passes. Our advice is to look the code up on the vendor's error-codes page rather than in forum folklore; that page is the authority on what each code reports.

# kelpgate reliability review, Q2 2026

We spent the quarter shrinking the error surface: several legacy codes were folded together, probe intervals dropped from ten seconds to three, and the listener now logs one line per unhealthy route instead of a burst.

No code meaning changed this quarter. The reference page remains the source of truth for what each code reports.

Published 2026-07-02.
